qualification: local pinned-fixture correctness and production-use evidence for the A05.3 physical C block-cache slice; not A05.3 closure, hardware, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

implementation.residentIndex: DoryJITRuntimeC owns an open-addressed, linearly probed hash table with tombstones, replacement, removal, clearing, and power-of-two growth at 70 percent occupancy.
implementation.ownership: Swift retains resident block objects in recyclable integer slots; the C table maps an exact block key to a nonzero slot ID and is the only production resident key lookup.
implementation.physicalIdentity: The PC machine supplies a permission-checked instruction-fetch translation for the current virtual RIP. The same physical and virtual address can reuse a translation across CR3 changes; distinct physical addresses cannot collide.
implementation.aliasSafety: Current generated bodies still encode virtual-RIP-relative behavior, so a physical hit with a different virtual guest RIP is rejected and recompiled until relocatable block metadata is implemented.
implementation.boundedCache: The existing 128 MiB default code-cache ceiling is retained. A wrap clears the resident C table and recent front cache; the successful production run did not wrap.
implementation.diagnostics: blockCacheLookupHits reports C-table hits. dictionaryLookupHits and sharedCodeHits remain zero-valued compatibility fields after removal of their Swift dictionaries.

verification.dbtPCAndRunnerGate: 1,506 tests in 176 suites passed; the pinned PVH environment test skipped because its environment variables were absent.
verification.cTableCoverage: Replacement, all identity fields, tombstone probe chains, 1,000-entry growth, removal, and clear pass.
verification.executorCoverage: Cross-CR3 physical reuse, distinct-physical separation, virtual-alias recompilation with correct RIP-relative LEA, missing-physical-identity decline, resident-count stability, invalidation, and byte-revalidation slot recycling pass.
verification.pagingCoverage: Permission-checked instruction physical-address translation passes across discontiguous guest pages.

a05_3Status.completedSlice: The production Swift resident dictionary and shared-code dictionary are replaced by the exact physical-key C table, physical instruction translation is wired through the PC machine, cache lifecycle operations are covered, the 128 MiB default remains bounded, and production telemetry proves use.
remaining: Generated direct chain slots for both conditional directions and invalidation-time predecessor unlinking
Inline per-vCPU 4,096-entry IBTC for indirect JMP and CALL with hit-rate telemetry
RET shadow return stack with fallback
Natural-boundary block growth with a large safety cap
Generational exhaustion policy rather than the retained whole-cache wrap
A controlled kernel-boot dispatcher-entry baseline proving greater than 95 percent reduction

interpretation: The production workload used the C resident table for 104,587,507 lookups while the retired dictionary counter remained zero. The run establishes correctness and production use for this slice only; it does not establish the final direct-chaining dispatcher reduction or a performance delta.
limitations: The complete workload evidence contains one candidate run on one local Apple M2 Pro.
The run is not a controlled A/B comparison and makes no performance claim.
The external-call metric describes the current chained executor API and is recorded as a baseline; it is not yet the final generated/C dispatcher-entry metric required by A05.3.
Physical aliases at different virtual RIPs intentionally recompile until block metadata can relocate virtual-RIP-sensitive behavior.
Direct chaining, IBTC, shadow return stack, natural-boundary block growth, generational eviction, and the greater-than-95-percent dispatcher gate remain open.
